Thank you for your interest in CSU Dominguez Hills! This articulation agreement displays lower-division course requirements specific to this major. Students are advised to meet with an academic counselor when planning to transfer to CSU Dominguez Hills and refer to the University Catalog to learn more about this major and its features. Detailed admissions requirements for transfer students are available on the CSUDH campus website. Completion of Statutory Requirements (United States History, Constitution and American Ideals) is a baccalaureate degree requirement for the California State University system and may be met prior to transfer with eligible California Community College (CCC) courses designated as US-1, US-2, and US-3. Completion of Statutory Requirements prior to transfer is most advantageous and strongly encouraged as a number of CCC courses that meet this requirement might also double-count for General Education.

Auditions: As an unimpacted department, acceptance auditions are currently not required. Incoming music majors should come prepared to meet or exceed the performance technical requirements of accredited music degrees on the student’s primary instrument, such as proficiency in the 12 major and minor scales. A placement audition is required for placement into the Music Liberal Arts option, Music Education option, or Bachelor of Music degree at California State University, Dominguez Hills. During the audition students will also be considered for scholarship awards.


Lower Division Ensemble Requirement: Students are required to complete a lower division ensemble course at the 100-level and 200-level in a fall semester and a spring semester. 100-level ensembles are to be chosen from: MUS 167, 168, 169, 170, 171, 172, 173, 175, 176, 177, and 178.


Additional Program information may be found in the Music Student Handbook 2024-2025.

The Bachelor of Music degree is a professional degree that prepares students for a variety of diverse careers in music. According to the National Association of Schools of Music, the national accrediting organization, the B.M. is a professional degree in which students are “expected to develop the knowledge, skills, concepts, and sensitivities essential to the professional life of the musician. To fulfill various professional responsibilities, the musician must exhibit not only technical competence, but also broad knowledge of music and music literature, the ability to integrate musical knowledge and skills sensitive to musical styles, and an insight into the role of music in intellectual and cultural life”.
